sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The async legacy write goroutines derive their context from the request ctx. WHY: that ctx is cancelled as soon as the HTTP handler returns, so the legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection is usually aborted, and legacy storage silently diverges from unified storage. HOW: detach cancellation with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (Go 1.21+) before applying the 10s timeout.

WHAT: A failed Storage.Create is recorded with recordLegacyDuration. WHY: unified-storage errors are attributed to the legacy metric, which skews both the storage and legacy dashboards. HOW: call recordStorageDuration(true, ...).
WHAT: A failed Storage.Update is recorded with recordLegacyDuration. WHY: unified-storage update errors are attributed to the legacy metric. HOW: use recordStorageDuration(true, ...).

WHAT: The success path of Delete passes `name` as the metric's kind/name label instead of options.Kind. WHY: this creates a high-cardinality label that differs from the error path, which uses options.Kind. HOW: pass options.Kind.

WHAT: The legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded with recordStorageDuration. WHY: legacy timings and errors are counted as storage metrics, which double-counts storage and hides legacy failures. HOW: use recordLegacyDuration.

Wrong metric labels are used in the dual-writer mode 3 changes. The reviewer noticed this as a bug outside their review class (security) and gave no further detail, so check that each metric is recorded with the correct label.
The Delete path builds its context using d.Log instead of the local log variable. Use log so that the logger carried in the context is consistent with the other code paths.

When Storage.Create fails, the code calls recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration. The failed storage call's duration and error are attributed to the legacy metric, so storage errors are miscounted.
When Storage.Update fails, the error is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, using the storage start time. The failure is attributed to the wrong backend in the metrics.
The legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded with recordStorageDuration. This mixes legacy timings into the storage metric and leaves the legacy metric empty for this method.

In Delete, the enriched `log` is built but the context is created from `d.Log`. This drops the name, kind and method values from the context logger. The success metric also passes `name` as the kind label, while every other call uses options.Kind. That creates a metric series per object name.

The old Mode3 Delete treated a NotFound from unified storage as non-fatal and still deleted from legacy storage. The new code returns on any storage error, including NotFound. An object that exists only in legacy storage, for example one not yet migrated, can no longer be deleted, and the request fails instead of cleaning up legacy. Restore the NotFound tolerance and continue to the legacy delete.

The legacy write used to run synchronously within the request. It now runs in a goroutine whose context is derived from the request ctx, which is cancelled as soon as the handler returns. The legacy create can therefore be cancelled mid-flight, and its failure is only recorded as a metric. Derive the goroutine's context with context.WithoutCancel(ctx) before applying the timeout. The same pattern appears in the Update, Delete and DeleteCollection goroutines.
In Delete, the metric is recorded with `name` where `kind` belongs. This puts per-object names into a metric label, which causes a metric cardinality problem. Pass `kind` as the label value instead.
Delete passes `d.Log` into the context instead of the local `log` logger. The request-scoped logger, with its added values, is therefore not used. Pass `log` instead.
When the storage Create fails, the code calls recordLegacyDuration. The failed call is to Storage, not Legacy, so the failure is recorded under the legacy metric. Use recordStorageDuration.

When the storage Update fails, the code calls recordLegacyDuration with the storage start time. The failure is recorded under the legacy metric even though the failing call is to Storage. Use recordStorageDuration.
The legacy DeleteCollection duration and result are recorded with recordStorageDuration. The call being timed is to Legacy, so they are attributed to the storage metric. Use recordLegacyDuration.

On a successful Delete, the `kind` argument is passed as `name` instead of `options.Kind`. Every other call uses `options.Kind` for this argument, so the metric gets one label value per object name instead of per kind.

The async legacy Create derives its context from the request ctx, which is cancelled as soon as the handler returns. The legacy write can be aborted mid-flight, leaving legacy storage without the object that unified storage already has. Derive the timeout context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx).

The async legacy Update uses a context derived from the request ctx, which is cancelled when the handler returns. The legacy update can be cancelled before it completes, leaving legacy storage stale relative to unified storage. Derive the timeout context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx).

The async legacy Delete uses a context derived from the request ctx, which is cancelled when the handler returns. The legacy delete can be aborted, so the object is deleted from unified storage but remains in legacy storage. Use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) as the parent of the timeout.

Mode 3 writes to legacy storage in a background goroutine, and none of the Create, Update, Delete or DeleteCollection tests wait for it or assert it. Removing the legacy call entirely would leave every test green. Use a synchronisation point (for example a channel closed by the mock's Run callback, or assert.Eventually with m.AssertCalled) to verify the legacy method is invoked.

The case is named "error when creating object in the unified store fails" but sets the failing Create expectation via setupLegacyFn, with no storage setup. It only passes because legacy and storage mocks share one mock.Mock, so it cannot tell which store's failure is propagated. Register the failure with setupStorageFn so the test targets the storage path it names.

issues.descricao: Delete puts the base d.Log instead of the enriched per-call logger into the context, so downstream logs lose name/kind/method fields.
issues.textoGolden: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.

comentarios.texto: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` installs the mode-level logger instead of the request-scoped `log` built on line 96 (which carries name, kind and method) — a copy/paste error, as every other method in this file passes the composed `log`. Storage.Delete and the legacy delete goroutine therefore log without the per-request fields this PR is adding (and without the metrics method/kind context).
ctx is built with klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of the enriched `log`. The delete logs then lose the name, kind and method values. Use `log`.
The Delete context uses d.Log rather than the per-call log. This is a logging-context inconsistency (not a data leak); use the per-call logger for consistency.

issues.descricao: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
issues.textoGolden: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.

comentarios.texto: The legacy DeleteCollection duration and error status are recorded in the unified-storage histogram. Every successful unified deletion therefore produces a second storage observation for a different backend, while legacy deletion failures are attributed to unified storage and no legacy observation is emitted. Call recordLegacyDuration here instead.

The timed call is d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, but its measurement is emitted using recordStorageDuration. Use recordLegacyDuration; otherwise storage receives two measurements for a successful collection deletion and legacy receives none, and legacy failures appear as storage failures.
The legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded with recordStorageDuration, so legacy latency and errors are attributed to storage. Use recordLegacyDuration.

issues.descricao: Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.

comentarios.texto: The Delete success-path metric passes `name` where every other call site in this file (lines 48, 103, 113, 156, 159) passes options.Kind in the kind/name argument slot. The storage-success sample for Delete is thus labelled with the object name instead of the resource kind, breaking label consistency with the other operations and with the error sample emitted at line 103. Use options.Kind here (or insert name consistently everywhere, matching the metric's label semantics).
recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) at line 106 passes the object name in the kind label slot.

recordStorageDuration is called with the object `name` as the `kind` label: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. Every other storage call site passes `options.Kind` (lines 73, 89, 103, 156, 159). This injects a per-object value into the kind label, corrupting the metric and giving it unbounded cardinality (one series per object name), which grows memory on every delete. Should be `options.Kind`.

issues.descricao: On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

comentarios.texto: On a Storage.Create failure the code records the error with recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) — the failing subsystem is Storage, not Legacy, and it passes the storage start time. This records storage failures under the legacy metric, corrupting the dual-writer error dashboards (and contradicts the success path on line 48 which uses recordStorageDuration). Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

On a Storage.Update failure the code records the error with recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage), attributing a storage failure and its storage duration to the legacy metric. This is inconsistent with the success path on line 132 (recordStorageDuration) and with mode1's semantics. Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

The async goroutine performing the LEGACY DeleteCollection measures it with d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). Every other legacy write in this file uses recordLegacyDuration (lines 56, 113, 140); recording it under the storage metric reports legacy latency/errors as storage latency/errors. Use d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).

issues.descricao: Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.

comentarios.texto: The async legacy write goroutine derives its context from the request-scoped `ctx` (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)). The apiserver cancels that context as soon as the HTTP handler returns — which is immediately after Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection return — so the goroutine's Legacy.Create can be canceled before completing, silently dropping the legacy write that this mode exists to guarantee. The same applies to the goroutines at lines 108-114, 134-141 and 161-167. Detach the async context from request cancellation (e.g. derive from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) / context.Background()) before applying the timeout.

The legacy write in Mode 3 became fire-and-forget, changing the contract callers relied on: previously Create (and, identically, Update/Delete/DeleteCollection) returned only after the LegacyStorage call had been made in-request; now it returns immediately and the write runs in a detached goroutine. Worse, the goroutine builds its context from the request-scoped `ctx` (line 51: `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`), which the API server cancels as soon as the handler returns/flushes the response — so the legacy write and its 10s timeout will typically be cancelled outright and the legacy store silently stops being updated, which is precisely what the new mode-3 integration cases assume still happens. Any detached work must be given a context not tied to the request lifetime (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a server-lifetime context), and consumers that depended on the synchronous legacy write need to be updated.

The asynchronous legacy write derives its timeout context from the request context, which is canceled when the HTTP request finishes. Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection return before this work completes, so their legacy database operations can be canceled immediately instead of receiving the intended ten-second window. Derive the bounded background context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) to retain request values without inheriting request cancellation.

issues.descricao: Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.

comentarios.texto: Legacy.Update receives the original objInfo instead of the object successfully committed to unified storage. The playlist legacy implementation calls objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old) against its own legacy object, so a patch is reapplied to potentially stale state and can persist a different result or fail rather than mirror the unified write. Pass an updateWrapper containing res, as the previous implementation did.

Legacy.Update previously received an updateWrapper containing the object returned by Storage.Update; it now receives the original objInfo. UpdatedObjectInfo can compute an update from the old object supplied by each backend (notably for patches), so evaluating it against a stale legacy object can produce a different result or reject an update that already succeeded in Storage. Preserve the canonical-result contract by passing an updateWrapper with updated: res and upstream: objInfo to the legacy consumer rather than replaying the original update against legacy state.

Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo rather than the updateWrapper containing the object successfully committed to Storage. UpdatedObjectInfo can represent a patch/transform based on the supplied old object; replaying it against legacy's potentially different old state can persist a different result or fail, even though the authoritative update succeeded. Restore forwarding of the committed result via updateWrapper instead of recomputing the update against legacy state.

issues.descricao: The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.

comentarios.texto: The legacy half of Mode 3 is never verified, so these tests cannot catch its removal. Mode 3 is documented as writing to BOTH LegacyStorage and Storage, and the implementation performs the legacy write in a detached goroutine (`go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`, dualwriter_mode3.go lines 50-57, and likewise at 108-114, 134-141, 161-167). Each test registers legacy expectations (`setupLegacyFn`, e.g. lines 30-32 and 40-42) but never calls `m.AssertExpectations(t)`, `AssertCalled` or `AssertNumberOfCalls`, and never waits for or observes the goroutine — no channel, no polling. Additionally `legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `storageMock{m, s}` (lines 53-54, and the same pair in every other test function) share one `*mock.Mock`, so even a count assertion could not distinguish a legacy call from a storage call. Deleting every `d.Legacy.*` call from the implementation leaves all six tests passing, which is exactly the regression the names — and the Mode 3 contract — claim to cover.

The successful Create test never verifies the legacy write. Configuring m.On("Create", ...) does not require that expectation to be consumed, and these assertions only inspect the object returned by Storage.Create. Deleting the entire legacy-create goroutine would still pass this test. Use distinct storage and legacy mocks and synchronize on the legacy call, then assert that it completed with the intended object.

The successful Update case configures a legacy Update expectation but returns after checking only the unified-store result. It neither waits for the asynchronous legacy update nor verifies its expectation, so removing the legacy-update goroutine entirely still passes. Add explicit synchronization and verification of the legacy update (ideally with separate mocks), including the object propagated to legacy storage.

issues.descricao: The List error test case is still named 'not implemented' although List is now implemented and the case checks storage error propagation.

comentarios.texto: The test-case name "error when listing an object in the unified store is not implemented" still describes the old stub List (which returned nil, nil with a "List not implemented" log). List is now implemented at dualwriter_mode3.go:79 and delegates to Storage.List; the case merely checks that a Storage error is propagated. The name contradicts the code it now exercises — rename it, e.g. "error when listing objects in the unified store fails".

issues.descricao: The Create test case name says 'only in the unified store' although Mode 3 also writes to legacy.

comentarios.texto: The test name says creation happens "only in the unified store", but this case configures a successful Legacy.Create as well, and Mode3.Create launches that legacy write after the unified write succeeds. Rename the case to describe creation in both stores (with the legacy write asynchronous), so test output does not communicate the opposite of the mode-3 write contract.

issues.descricao: Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.

comentarios.texto: Independent goroutines remove ordering between successful writes to the same resource. For example, Storage commits update A and then update B, but the legacy goroutine for B can finish before A, leaving legacy with A while Storage contains B. Likewise a delete can run before an earlier create and leave a resurrected legacy object. Preserve per-resource commit order for mirroring (including across create/update/delete), rather than launching each write independently.

issues.descricao: The storage-failure Create test registers its failing expectation via setupLegacyFn and only works because legacy and storage share one mock.

comentarios.texto: The 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' case registers the failing Create expectation only through setupLegacyFn. It passes only because legacy and storage share one mock, so the storage Create gets that error by accident. Register the expectation in setupStorageFn and use separate mocks for legacy and storage, so the test really covers a storage failure.

issues.descricao: DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The migration reads `execute(...)[0]['id']` and `[0]['value']` without checking for an empty result. WHY: When no `embed_category` site setting row exists (the default for most sites), the INNER JOIN returns zero rows, so `[0]` is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError and aborts. The `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15 can fail the same way. HOW: Use `.first`/`ntuples` guards with nil-safe access and fall back to a default category.

WHAT: `record_for_host` compares `uri.host` against `lower(host)` without downcasing the URI host. It also drops the port. WHY: A referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/x` never matches the stored lowercase host, and hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) can never match because `URI#host` excludes the port, so embedding is denied. HOW: Use `host.downcase`, and match on the host plus the port when the stored value includes one.

WHAT: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!` without handling a nil host. WHY: A create/update request with a missing `host` param (or a record with a nil host) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. HOW: Guard with `if host.present?` or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

WHAT: `update` and `destroy` use `.where(id: ...).first` and call methods on the result without a nil check. WHY: An unknown or already-deleted id gives a nil record, so `host.destroy` or `save_host(nil)` raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404. HOW: Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` (404 on a missing record) or raise Discourse::NotFound.

The query lowercases the stored host with lower(host) but compares it to the URI host without lowercasing it. A referer or embed URL such as http://EvilTrout.com never matches an allowed host, so legitimate embeds are rejected. Downcase the incoming host before the comparison.

The test "is false if embeddable_host is blank" does not set `embed_truncate` to true or stub `has_topic_embed?`, so `expandable_first_post?` is false from the defaults (`embed_truncate` false). It would pass whatever the embeddable host state is, and so verifies nothing about hosts. Remove it, since the host check no longer exists, or rename it and give it the setup that makes the true case pass so it checks what its name says.

The migration indexes `[0]` on query results that can be empty. When `embed_category` is unset or has no matching category, or when `uncategorized_category_id` is not stored in site_settings, `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. This aborts the migration on a default install. Use `.first` or check `cmd_tuples > 0` before indexing, and fall back to the default category id.

The fabricator files are swapped. embeddable_host_fabricator.rb now holds the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators, while category_fabricator.rb holds the :embeddable_host fabricator. The file names no longer match their contents, which misleads anyone looking for a fabricator. Restore category_fabricator.rb to its original content and put the :embeddable_host fabricator in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

The test is named "is false if embeddable_host is blank", but Topic#expandable_first_post? no longer checks embeddable hosts. It now returns false only because has_topic_embed? is false, so the name describes behaviour the code no longer has. Rename it to reflect that it covers the case with no topic embed, or remove it.

The migration indexes `execute(...)[0]['id']` without checking for an empty result. When no `embed_category` setting row matches a category, which is the default, `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The migration then aborts. Fetch the first row and treat nil as 0 so the fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` runs.

The before_validation callback calls `self.host.sub!` with no nil guard. A create or update request without a host param leaves host nil, so the callback raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard against nil before the substitution.

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id. `update` then calls `host.host=` on nil and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil, so both raise NoMethodError and return a 500. Use `find` so a missing record gives a proper not-found response.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally, so saving a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.
issues.textoGolden: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: The before_validation callback calls `sub!` on host without guarding nil. Creating a host with a missing or null host field reaches this callback from save_host and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard nil during normalization and let presence/format validation reject it.

WHAT: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally, so a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError (`nil.sub!`) instead of producing a normal format-invalid result. WHY: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly; any request that omits the host value makes the save raise a 500 instead of returning the `render_json_error(host)` validation response. HOW: guard the mutation, e.g. `return if host.blank?` at the top of the before_validation block (or use `self.host = self.host.to_s` before stripping).

before_validation calls self.host.sub!(...) on a possibly-nil host before validates_format_of runs. The controller assigns host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host], so a request without a host key leaves it nil and nil.sub! raises NoMethodError at save time instead of the format validation producing a normal error response. Add a presence guard so validation reports the failure.

issues.descricao: update and destroy in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController fetch the host with where(id:).first and never check for nil, so an unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of not-found.
issues.textoGolden: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: In the destroy action, the nil-host case (line 15-16) would raise NoMethodError. Consider adding a nil check to handle the case where the host is not found.

update and destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first but never check for nil, then immediately use it (save_host(host) does host.host = ... / host.save; destroy does host.destroy). A stale or already-deleted id, or an interleaving where a concurrent delete removes the row first, makes host nil and the first call on it raises NoMethodError -> unhandled 500. Guard with a nil/404 check before use.

Update passes the nullable result of where(...).first directly to save_host, which immediately assigns host.host. Updating a nonexistent or concurrently deleted record returns an internal error instead of a not-found response; destroy has the same lookup failure. Use find or explicitly raise a not-found error before dereferencing the lookup result.

issues.descricao: record_for_host compares lower(host) against the un-lowercased URI host, so mixed-case referer hosts fail to match allowed hosts and embedding is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Normalize the parsed hostname before comparing it with lower(host). URI parsing preserves hostname case, so an allowed entry such as example.com does not match https://EXAMPLE.com/page even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This makes valid embedding requests fail the host authorization check and makes category lookup inconsistent for equivalent domain identities. Compare against host.downcase (or normalize both operands equivalently), and add a mixed-case URL test.

The query compares lower(host) to the un-downcased uri.host. A referer such as http://EvilTrout.com never matches the stored lowercase host, so embedding is wrongly denied. Fix: use where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).

The query compares lower(host) in the database with uri.host, which is not lowercased, so the comparison normalizes only one side. A referer or URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com) will not match the stored host. Compare against host.downcase, i.e. where('lower(host) = ?', host.downcase).

issues.descricao: The migration copies the legacy embeddable_hosts values into the new table without stripping scheme and path, so hosts stored as http://example.com no longer match the bare-host lookup and previously allowed embeds are rejected after upgrade.
issues.textoGolden: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration inserts raw embeddable_hosts lines (e.g. http://example.com/123) without stripping scheme/path like the model does. WHY: migrated rows never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host which compares bare uri.host, silently breaking previously allowed embeds.

Migration INSERTs raw embeddable_hosts lines with scheme/path intact, but EmbeddableHost normalizes to bare domain (before_validation strips protocol/path, record_for_host looks up by URI.host). Strip protocol and path before INSERT or migrated hosts will never satisfy host_allowed?.

Legacy hosts are inserted verbatim instead of applying the new model's scheme/path normalization. Existing values such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 remain in the table, while record_for_host compares only URI.host, so previously configured embedding hosts stop working after upgrade. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the model before inserting them.

issues.descricao: The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped, so each file defines the other's fabricators.
issues.textoGolden: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

comentarios.texto: File named category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while Fabricator(:category) was moved to embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Filenames disagree with contents — swap contents back so each file defines the fabricator its name states.

The file names and contents are swapped. embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category), and category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host. Restore category_fabricator.rb to the original category fabricators and put the :embeddable_host fabricator in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

issues.descricao: The migration builds its INSERT by interpolating each legacy host value into the SQL string instead of quoting or binding it, so a value with a quote breaks the statement.
issues.textoGolden: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

comentarios.texto: The migration's INSERT statement uses string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). This is a SQL-injection concern and should be fixed by using parameterized queries or proper escaping.
WHAT: migration interpolates raw host string into SQL: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). WHY: a host value containing a single quote breaks the statement and allows SQL injection via site_settings value.

issues.descricao: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.
issues.textoGolden: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] with no guard when embed_category setting/category is missing. WHY: nil[0] dereference crashes the migration and blocks deploy on instances without that setting.
Migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking empty result; missing site_settings row throws NoMethodError and fails migration. Check for nil row.

The migration indexes the first category-query result before checking whether any row was returned. An installation without a persisted embed_category setting, or with no matching category name, aborts migration before reaching the uncategorized fallback. Check whether the result contains a row before accessing its id and handle missing fallback settings as well.

issues.descricao: The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer sets up any host condition and passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, so its name no longer matches what it tests.

comentarios.texto: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' does not establish the true-branch preconditions (embed_truncate true, has_topic_embed true) nor control host presence, so it passes regardless of host logic and would still pass if host checking were broken/removed. Set truncate true + stub embed true with no hosts for the false case.

The test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now uses an ordinary built topic without setting embed_truncate or making has_topic_embed? true. It therefore returns false for reasons unrelated to the missing host, and passes even with the new implementation that never checks host availability. If blank-host behavior remains the intended contract, arrange all the other prerequisites before asserting false; if the contract intentionally changed, replace this case with a test of the actual intended behavior rather than retaining a misleading passing test.

The description "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer matches the code. This PR changed Topic#expandable_first_post? (app/models/topic.rb:869) to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing the embeddable_hosts condition entirely, and removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` setup from this test. The assertion now passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is unstubbed (false) and embed_truncate is unset, so the name states a cause the method no longer has — rename it (e.g. "is false when there is no topic embed") or set up the precondition it claims to test.

issues.descricao: The 'find embedded' test requests fruit 2 but the pretender always returns fruit 1, so it asserts fruit 1's colors and would not notice a find that ignores the id.

comentarios.texto: Test requests fruit id 2 but pretender returns fruits[0] unconditionally, so assertions on colors [1,2] never cover fruit 2's color_ids [3]. Make pretender honor :id or request id 1 / assert single-element case to actually verify plural _ids hydration.

This test now requests fruit 2 but expects fruit 1's two colors. The /fruits/:id Pretender handler always returns fruits[0], so the test passes while hydrating the wrong record and would not catch a find implementation that ignores the requested ID. Make the handler select the requested fruit and assert its ID and corresponding colors (fruit 2 has only color 3), or request fruit 1 if testing its two-color hydration is the goal.

issues.descricao: After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.

comentarios.texto: The save callback overwrites the category using categoryId even when the server substituted the uncategorized category for a blank selection. Adding a host without choosing a category therefore leaves its category badge empty, and editing it reads an undefined category id despite a valid category_id having been returned. Resolve the category from the saved response's category_id rather than the submitted selection.

When categoryId is null (the default for a new row, or a cleared selection), the controller saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that category_id. This callback instead overwrites host.category with findById(null), making the displayed category disagree with the saved category. Use the category from the save response or its returned category_id rather than the pre-save selection.

Use the saved response's category rather than overwriting it from categoryId after saving. For a new host with no category selected, categoryId is null, while the new controller deliberately saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that ID through the serializer. This callback replaces the hydrated category with findById(null), leaving the row without its actual category until reload (and reopening edit also initializes from that incorrect relationship).

issues.descricao: Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.

comentarios.texto: Host lookup compares URI.host against a stored value that validation explicitly permits to include a port. Saving example.com:8080 succeeds, but a request from http://example.com:8080 produces URI.host equal to example.com and never matches that record, disabling embedding and retrieval for the configured host. Use a consistent port representation in both storage and lookup.

The validator accepts hosts such as `example.com:8080`, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host (`example.com`) and compares it to the stored port-qualified string. An accepted and saved host therefore never authorizes its corresponding URLs. Normalize the stored and queried authority consistently, including a deliberate port policy.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The working-hours check compares the UTC day and minutes of the slot against workingHours that are in the host's own timezone, and `end` duplicates `start`. WHY: Hosts outside UTC get valid slots rejected or invalid ones accepted, and the end of the slot is never checked. Separately, `find` returns true as soon as the slot is outside any single working-hours entry, so a host with several entries loses slots that another entry covers. HOW: Convert the slot to the host's timezone (`time.tz(organizerTimeZone)`) before reading day/hour/minute. Compute `end` from `slotEndTime`. Reject the slot only if no entry for that day contains it, for example with `some` to find a containing entry and a separate check that entries exist for that day.

WHAT: `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares object references and is always false, so the zero-length override branch (an override that blocks the whole day) is dead code. WHY: A zero-length override that marks the day unavailable is not honoured, and the slot falls through as available whenever it is on that day. HOW: Compare with `.isSame(...)`.

WHAT: The date-override check only rejects a slot if its end is at or before the override start, or its start is after the override end. It never rejects a slot that starts inside the override and ends after the override end, and it does not reject a slot that starts before the override start and ends inside it. WHY: Slots straddling the override boundary, for example 10:30-11:30 on a 10-11 override, stay bookable even though they extend past the host's overridden availability. HOW: Require the slot to lie fully within the override, with slotStart >= overrideStart and slotEnd <= overrideEnd.

The variable `end` is named as the slot end, but it is computed from `slotStartTime`, so it always equals `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` check therefore never tests the slot's real end. Compute `end` from `slotEndTime` so the value matches its name.

getSlots now depends on `override.timeZone`, but the shared TimeRange type declares it optional and only getSchedule was updated to populate it. Any other dateOverrides caller that omits timeZone gets `.tz(undefined)`, which does not fall back to the organizer's zone, so the offset is computed wrongly and override slots shift. Make the dependency explicit (a required field on the override type, or a defined fallback such as organizerTimeZone) and update the remaining callers.

The new +6:00 date-override test expects the same UTC slots as the +5:30 case. The pre-change code, which used UTC hours and ignored the invitee timezone, also returns those slots, so the test would pass if the offset logic in slots.ts were reverted. Use a timezone and override combination where the old and new logic produce different slots, and assert the offset-aware result.
Two dayjs objects are compared with `===`, which compares references and is always false. The branch meant to mark a zero-length (day off) override as unavailable can never run. Use `.isSame()`.

`end` is computed with the same expression as `start` (slotStartTime), so `end > workingHour.endTime` just repeats the start comparison. Slots that begin inside working hours but run past the end are not rejected. Compute `end` from slotEndTime.

The working-hours check computes `end` from slotStartTime, so `end` equals `start`. The slot's end is never compared with workingHour.endTime, so slots that run past the end of working hours are accepted. Compute `end` from slotEndTime (`slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()`).

The date-override boundary checks are wrong. The check at line 123 only compares the slot start with the override end, so a slot that starts before the override end but ends after it is accepted. The `===` on dayjs objects at line 114 is reference equality and never true. Reject when `slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)` and compare with `.isSame()`.

The working-hours check is wrong. `find` returns true when a slot is outside any one working-hour entry, so a day with split hours (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17) rejects every slot. `end` is also computed from the slot start rather than `slotEndTime`, so the slot's end is never checked. Use `some` to test whether the slot fits inside any entry, compute `end` from the slot end time, and reject only if none contain it.
Two dayjs objects are compared with `===`, which compares object references and is always false. The zero-length-override branch can never run. Compare with `.isSame()` instead.

issues.descricao: The working-hours check computes end from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so slots that start within working hours but end after them are accepted.
issues.textoGolden: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` — an exact duplicate of `start` — instead of using `slotEndTime`. WHY: the working-hours upper-bound test `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore compares the slot START against the working-day end, so a slot whose start is inside working hours but whose end (start + eventLength) overruns `workingHour.endTime` is never filtered and is reported as available, allowing bookings outside the host's working hours. HOW: compute `const end = slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute();`.

`end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so it always equals `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` check is identical to the `start` check and never catches a slot that starts within working hours but ends past them. Use `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()` for `end`.

`end` is computed identically to `start` (both from slotStartTime), so the check `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` can never reject a slot on the upper bound. A slot starting inside working hours but ending after workingHour.endTime is wrongly considered available; derive `end` from slotEndTime instead.

issues.descricao: The date-override check compares two dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, so zero-length (day off) overrides are never detected.
issues.textoGolden: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

comentarios.texto: This compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with `===` (reference equality), which is always false, so a zero-length override (start equal to end, whole day blocked) never returns true here. Compare timestamps, e.g. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))`.

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separate dayjs object references, so `===` is always false. The zero-length date-override branch is dead code and such an override is never recognised as covering the day; compare values (e.g. .isSame() or .valueOf() === .valueOf()) instead.

The equality check compares two separately created Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, even when the override start and end represent the same instant. The intended zero-length/closed-day rejection is unreachable, and a slot beginning exactly at that instant can reach the dateOverrideExist success return. Compare timestamps or use isSame instead.

issues.descricao: When a date override exists for the day, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking busy times, so slots overlapping existing bookings are reported available.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: when `dateOverrideExist` is true the function returns `true` before running the `busy.every(...)` check at the end. WHY: on any day that has a matching date override, a slot inside the override is reported available without checking the host's existing bookings (`busy` is spread via `...schedule`/`...userSchedule`), so a fixed/loose host who already has a booking during the override window is still shown as free — enabling double-booking. HOW: do not return early here; fall through so the override branch only decides whether the slot is inside the override window, and let the existing `busy` evaluation decide availability (e.g. `if (dateOverrideExist) { /* within override, still check busy */ } else { /* fall through to busy */ }`).

The new `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` short-circuits the `busy` conflict check (and the workingHours check) for any slot that falls inside a date override window. Every caller of `checkIfIsAvailable` previously counted on it returning false for a slot that overlaps an existing booking; on days covered by a date override that guarantee is gone, so slots conflicting with the user's real bookings are now reported as available and can be double-booked. The override branch should let control fall through to the `busy.every(...)` check (returning true only for the availability-window part) instead of returning early.

A matching date override returns true before checking busy periods. Both fixed-host and loose-host callers pass calendar and booking conflicts in busy, so a host with an override is offered even when an existing booking overlaps the slot. Continue to the busy checks after validating the override instead of returning true.

issues.descricao: The working-hours check rejects a slot when any interval for the weekday excludes it, so split schedules (e.g. morning and afternoon) reject all slots.

comentarios.texto: The working-hours predicate rejects a slot if any interval on its weekday does not contain it. A split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 therefore loses every slot, since each valid slot lies outside the other interval. Require at least one matching interval to contain the full event instead of finding an interval that excludes it.

This search rejects a slot if it falls outside any working-hours window on that weekday. With split hours of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a valid 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon window. Check for containment in at least one applicable window rather than finding any window that excludes the slot.

WHAT: Outside-working-hours test uses workingHours.find() returning true if ANY entry rejects the slot. WHY: With split schedules (two entries same weekday, e.g. morning+afternoon) a valid morning slot is outside the afternoon entry, find() matches and the slot is wrongly rejected as outside hours. HOW: Invert logic to accept if ANY entry contains the slot (e.g. !workingHours.some(entry contains slot) => outside).

issues.descricao: The date-override bound compares the slot start, not the slot end, with the override end, so slots extending past the override are accepted.

comentarios.texto: The override bounds reject only non-overlapping slots rather than requiring the entire event to fit inside an override. A fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 10:30–11:30 event generated from another host's availability, despite being unavailable for its final half hour. Accept only when at least one override contains both slotStartTime and slotEndTime; this also avoids rejecting a slot merely because another interval on the same date does not overlap it.

The upper bound checks whether slotStartTime is after the override end. A slot that starts before the override end but finishes after it is treated as available. Compare slotEndTime with the override end using isAfter, so the slot must fit entirely inside the override.

issues.descricao: The override timezone conversion keeps only hour and minute, so overrides that cross midnight in the invitee timezone become inverted ranges or are applied to the wrong day.

comentarios.texto: Timezone conversion takes only hour and minute, discarding day rollover and turning intervals crossing attendee midnight into reversed ranges. A UTC organizer's 22:00–23:00 override viewed in UTC+01:30 becomes startTime 1410 and endTime 30, which buildSlots skips because start is greater than end, removing valid availability. Preserve the converted dates and split the interval across attendee-day boundaries before building slots.

WHAT: activeOverrides are filtered by UTC day (line 206-207) before the invitee/organizer offset is applied (lines 212-224), and shifted hours are not re-bucketed across midnight. WHY: An override that shifts to the previous/next calendar day in the invitee timezone is dropped from the wrong day or applied to the wrong day, so slots show open when the organizer is off (and vice versa). HOW: Filter/bucket overrides in the invitee-local date after applying the offset, or emit split entries spanning two invitee days.

issues.descricao: The new working-hours check does not reject slots on weekdays that have no working-hours entry, so those slots are treated as available.

comentarios.texto: A weekday with no matching working-hours entry falls through to the busy checks and is treated as available when there are no conflicts. In round-robin events, slots generated for a loose host can consequently include a fixed host whose schedule excludes that day. Reject slots unless a working-hours interval on the slot's weekday contains the event, when no date override applies.

issues.descricao: checkIfIsAvailable's date-override check never rejects a slot that starts before the override start (only one that ends before it), so slots partly outside the override hours are treated as available.

The override day is computed with local-time dayjs(date.start) while the slot day is formatted in UTC, so on a server not running in UTC overrides near midnight are applied to the wrong day or skipped.
With several date-override ranges on the same day, a slot is rejected as soon as it falls outside any one of them, so slots inside the other ranges become unavailable.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil and `tu.notification_level` is called on it without a guard. WHY: a user who has no topic_users row for the topic (for example one who was emailed after a category watch but never opened the topic) gets a NoMethodError and a 500 when they click the unsubscribe link. HOW: use `TopicUser.get` or `find_or_initialize_by`, or change the level with `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row.

WHAT: the unsubscribe action toggles the level without being idempotent. A level above regular goes to regular, and anything else goes to muted. WHY: reloading the page, retrying the request, or a client or security scanner that prefetches the emailed GET link moves the user from regular to muted, which silences the topic more than they asked for. The same request is also made from a state-changing GET. HOW: set the level to regular when it is above regular and leave it unchanged otherwise, or require an explicit POST or confirmation for muting.

`TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic, so `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link returns a 500. Create the row if it is missing, for example with `find_or_initialize_by`, or raise a NotFound before dereferencing it.

The fixture now passes `unsubscribe_url`, but no test asserts that the topic unsubscribe link appears in the body. The tests still only check the List-Unsubscribe header and the user preferences URL. If the per-topic unsubscribe link were removed from the `unsubscribe_link` locale or from the template args, every test here would still pass. Add an assertion such as `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.body).to include("/t/1234/unsubscribe")`.

The notification emails now link every recipient to this action. It assumes a TopicUser row exists for the user and topic. `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user was notified through a category watch or a default notification level and has no row. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError, so the unsubscribe link returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change` or `find_or_initialize_by`, or handle nil by creating the row with the new level.

The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only the notification mailer in user_notifications.rb passes `unsubscribe_url`. Any other email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` and no `unsubscribe_url` (e.g. the digest) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when the body is built. Put the topic-specific sentence in a separate string that is added only when `unsubscribe_url` is present, or give the other callers a URL.

`TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no TopicUser row for this topic, so `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link returns a 500. Handle the nil case, for example with `TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by`, before comparing the notification level.

TopicUser.find_by can return nil when the user has no topic_users row for this topic. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and the endpoint returns a 500. Use TopicUser.change, or create the row, instead of dereferencing a possibly nil record.

The GET action picks the new level from the current one: above regular goes to regular, otherwise it goes to muted. It is therefore not idempotent. A second visit, such as a refresh or a mail-client link prefetch, silently mutes a user who only meant to drop to regular. Set one deterministic target level, or require a POST.

The `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but `template_args` has no default for it. Any email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true and no unsubscribe_url option raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument from `body` and `html_part`. Provide a default (or make the string conditional) so existing callers keep working.

issues.descricao: The new unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level on a plain GET request, so a third-party page can trigger it for a logged-in user without any CSRF token.

comentarios.texto: The unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification_level (tu.save!) via a plain GET route (config/routes.rb:440-441) with skip_before_filter :check_xhr, authenticating only through the session cookie. There is no CSRF token (Rails forgery protection does not cover GET) and no capability token, unlike EmailController#unsubscribe which authorizes via DigestUnsubscribeKey. Any third-party page can embed and, when a logged-in user loads it, silently change that user's notification_level for the topic. Require a per-user capability token (like the digest unsubscribe key) in the URL, or perform the state change from an authenticated non-GET request that carries the CSRF token.

The new GET routes mutate the authenticated user's notification preferences without CSRF verification. An attacker can navigate a logged-in user's browser to a known topic unsubscribe URL and reduce or mute its notifications, because Rails excludes GET from forgery-token checks and unsubscribe explicitly skips check_xhr. Make GET render a confirmation page and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST or PUT.

WHAT: The unsubscribe state change (lowering/muting notification_level + save!) runs on a GET route (config/routes.rb GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe). WHY: An attacker can forge the URL as an image/prefetch/link to silently change a victim's notification state with no CSRF token since GETs are not CSRF-protected. HOW: Make the mutation a PUT/POST with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation parameter/token instead of mutating on page view.

issues.descricao: TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences TopicUser.find_by without handling a missing row, so users with no topic_users record get a NoMethodError/500 instead of being unsubscribed.
issues.textoGolden: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash

comentarios.texto: tu is not checked for nil before use. TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) returns nil whenever the logged-in user has no topic_users row for that topic (the same lookup TopicUser.get performs), and the next line dereferences tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. Because the route is only gated by ensure_logged_in, any logged-in user can hit /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe(.json) for a topic they never opened and trigger the crash. Guard the lookup, e.g. `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...); return render json: {success: false} unless tu` (or build/return early) before reading notification_level.

`TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return nil (e.g. the user clicks the emailed unsubscribe link for a topic for which no TopicUser row was ever created), and the very next line dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, then `tu.save!`). This raises NoMethodError on nil and the unsubscribe request 500s. Guard the nil case (e.g. return early or use `TopicUser.change`/`find_or_create_by`) before reading/writing notification_level.

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (find_by yields nil when no row exists), but the next lines dereference it unconditionally (`tu.notification_level`, `tu.save!`). Since the new unsubscribe routes are public GET endpoints, any logged-in user visiting /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe for a topic they have never tracked will trigger a NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a sane response. Guard the nil case (e.g. create/skip or redirect) before reading notification_level.

issues.descricao: The message builder spec passes unsubscribe_url in the fixture but never asserts the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the email.

comentarios.texto: The `unsubscribe_url` added to the `message_with_unsubscribe` fixture is never asserted. The two tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header `be_present` and that the body matches `user_preferences_url`; neither references `unsubscribe_url`. So they would still pass if the topic-specific unsubscribe URL this PR introduces were dropped or wired to the wrong value. Add an assertion (e.g. that `message_with_unsubscribe.body` matches `/t/1234/unsubscribe`, and that the List-Unsubscribe header points at the topic unsubscribe URL) so the new behaviour is actually covered.

The fixture now passes unsubscribe_url, but no assertion reads it. The tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body contains user_preferences_url, so they pass if the topic unsubscribe link is removed or broken. Add an assertion that the body includes "/t/1234/unsubscribe".

issues.descricao: The unsubscribe confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but watching/tracking users are only moved to regular, which still sends mention/reply notifications.

comentarios.texto: The confirmation promises that the user will stop receiving notifications for this topic, but TopicsController#unsubscribe sets watching/tracking users to regular, not muted. Regular still allows mention/reply notifications, so this confirmation (and the corresponding promise in the new email link text) overstates what clicking the link accomplished. Describe stopping notifications for every new post, or make the confirmation conditional on the resulting notification level so only muted users are told that all topic notifications have stopped.

issues.descricao: Unsubscribe saves the new notification level without setting notifications_reason_id, so auto-tracked topics are promoted back to tracking on the next read, undoing the unsubscribe.

comentarios.texto: Saving the notification level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged instead of recording an explicit user choice. For automatically tracked topics with a null reason, TopicUser.update_last_read promotes the row back to tracking when the reading threshold is exceeded, undoing the unsubscribe on the next read. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at are set consistently with set_notifications.

Saving the notification level directly bypasses the explicit-user-change metadata set by TopicUser.change. In particular, a topic_user with notifications_reason_id == nil remains eligible for TopicUser.auto_track, which checks that field and can promote the topic back to tracking after the user unsubscribes. Use the notification-change helper (or set its user-change reason and timestamp consistently) so the unsubscribe is retained as an explicit user preference.

issues.descricao: Claims the client unsubscribe route never performs the unsubscribe when entered through an in-app transition.

comentarios.texto: The client unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view and never performs the unsubscribe operation. When entered through an in-app transition rather than a full server navigation, PostStream.loadTopicView requests /t/:id.json (or consumes preload data), so the page claims notifications will stop while the persisted notification level remains unchanged. Ensure this entry path executes the unsubscribe operation before showing confirmation.

The client route loads the topic but never invokes the unsubscribe action. Notification levels are changed only by TopicsController#unsubscribe, so navigating to this route inside the Ember application can display “You will stop receiving notifications” without changing the subscription. Explicitly perform the unsubscribe operation on client-side entry rather than relying on the initial HTML request to have done it.

issues.descricao: The property name stopNotificiationsText is misspelled (should be stopNotificationsText).
issues.textoGolden: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

issues.descricao: The topic unsubscribe GET endpoint is not idempotent: each visit steps the notification level down again, so reloading the link moves a topic from regular to muted.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `forEach(async ...)` runs `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` in callbacks that nothing awaits, so the surrounding try/catch no longer catches their failures. WHY: A rejection from the calendar or video delete becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being logged, and the deletes can still be running when the function returns. HOW: Replace the forEach with a `for...of` loop that awaits each delete inside the try block, or use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

WHAT: `forEach(async ...)` runs `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` in callbacks that nothing awaits, so the surrounding try/catch no longer catches their failures. WHY: A rejection from the calendar or video delete becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being logged, and the deletes can still be running when the function returns. HOW: Use a `for...of` loop with `await` inside the try block, or `await Promise.all(map(...))`.

WHAT: The request-reschedule mutation uses `forEach(async ...)`, so the calendar and video deletions are fire-and-forget. WHY: Any failure in `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled rejection. The mutation can also return while the old events still exist, and in serverless runtimes the work can be cut off. HOW: Await the deletions with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop.

WHAT: The `appStore` object literal calls `import()` for all 30 apps as soon as the module is evaluated, so every app is still loaded eagerly. WHY: The PR gets none of the lazy-loading benefit. A failed import also becomes a permanently rejected cached promise, and nothing handles that rejection if no caller awaits it. HOW: Store loader functions such as `() => import("./zoomvideo")` and call only the one needed, for example `await appStore[key]()`.

Making the `forEach` callback async means the promises it returns are discarded. Rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections, and the reschedule handler continues before the calendar events are deleted. Collect the promises (for example with `map`) and `await Promise.all(...)` inside the try block.

getCalendar is now async, and this caller awaits it inside a `forEach(async ...)` callback. forEach ignores the returned promises, so the calendar deleteEvent calls are not awaited. The reschedule flow can finish before the events are deleted, and a failed deletion becomes an unhandled rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding try/catch. Collect the promises with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or use a for...of loop.

getCalendar is now awaited inside a forEach(async ...) callback. The surrounding try/catch no longer sees failures from getCalendar or from the dynamic app import, and forEach does not wait for the callbacks, so a failure becomes an unhandled rejection. Collect the promises with map and await them (for example Promise.all) inside the try block.

getCalendarCredentials now returns calendar as a Promise<Calendar | null> because getCalendar became async and is not awaited here. Any consumer of getCalendarCredentials other than getConnectedCalendars that uses .calendar directly will get a Promise. Await getCalendar here, or make the function async, so the returned shape stays the same.

issues.descricao: Async callbacks passed to forEach after getCalendar became async are never awaited, so calendar and video cancellations run fire-and-forget, may not finish, and their errors escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections.
issues.textoGolden: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

comentarios.texto: The async forEach callback moves calendar factory exceptions outside the surrounding try/catch because forEach discards its returned promise. An invalid encrypted Exchange credential throws during CalendarService construction, now producing an unhandled rejection while Reschedule continues and returns success instead of logging the error; the identical regression occurs in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts. Await Promise.all over bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...) inside the try block, or use an awaited for...of loop, so factory and deletion failures reach the catch.

The new async forEach callback is not awaited. If getCalendar rejects (for example, the dynamically imported calendar module fails to load or its service constructor throws), the callback produces a rejected promise that forEach discards; the surrounding try/catch cannot catch it. Previously a synchronous getCalendar failure reached that catch. Await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) or use an awaited for...of loop so these failures remain handled and calendar cleanup completes before rescheduling continues. Apply the same fix to the equivalent changed loop in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

WHAT: credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { await getCalendar; apiDeletes.push(...) }) pushes to apiDeletes asynchronously after outer code consumes it. WHY: outer apiDeletes is awaited elsewhere while async callbacks have not yet pushed, so recurring-event deletions are lost/partial and errors are unobserved. HOW: replace with for...of with await or collect promises via map + await Promise.all.

issues.descricao: Each import(...) in the appStore object literal runs when app-store/index.ts is imported, so all integrations still load at startup instead of lazily, while every entry becomes a promise.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The deleteCache mutation does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query and relies only on the optional `onSuccess` prop to refresh. WHY: If the parent passes no `onChanged`, or its handler does not refetch, the UI keeps showing the stale "Last updated" status and the delete action after the cache has been deleted. HOW: Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the mutation's onSuccess or onSettled, as `disconnectMutation` does.

WHAT: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only syntax. WHY: On Linux with GNU sed, `''` is treated as an input file name and the in-place edit fails, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated when it already exists in the env file. HOW: Write to a temp file and move it over the original, or detect the sed flavor.

The user query's selectedCalendars select now includes the internal Google webhook identifier `googleChannelId`, which no UI code in this PR uses. If this query's result is returned to the client (for example by the `me` handler), the identifier is exposed in the response. Drop `googleChannelId` from this shared select, or strip it before the result leaves the server.

The cache timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded "en-US" locale, while the surrounding text is translated through t(). Users with a non-English UI language see a US-style date and time inside a localised sentence. Use the user's locale from useLocale (i18n.language) in Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of the literal "en-US".

The migration's warning header says the column is added without a default and that this is not possible for a non-empty table. The SQL below adds it with DEFAULT NOW(), so the header contradicts the statement it describes. Remove or correct the stale warning.

When the credential is missing or not owned by the user, the handler throws a plain Error, which tRPC reports as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. Throw a TRPCError with code NOT_FOUND (or FORBIDDEN) so the response reflects the actual failure.

The comment says SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is bumped, but the call passes empty `data`, so it may issue no UPDATE. The UI's "last updated" value comes from CalendarCache.updatedAt, and nothing in this PR reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. The call and the select additions for `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` are dead work. Remove them, or set an explicit `updatedAt: new Date()` if the value is really needed.

issues.descricao: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId with an empty data object, so Prisma does not refresh the @updatedAt timestamp and SelectedCalendar.updatedAt never reflects the cache refresh.
issues.textoGolden: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {} to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. WHY: Prisma updateMany rejects empty data (validation error) or no-ops without touching @updatedAt, so the refresh path throws or silently leaves updatedAt stale. HOW: pass an explicit touch field e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() }.

Comment claims "Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt" but call passes empty object {} as data, so nothing is updated (Prisma updateMany with empty data is a no-op/error). Fix comment or pass { updatedAt: new Date() } to match the stated intent.

updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {}. Prisma updateMany throws when data is empty, so this line throws on every resync after the cache write. Pass an explicit touch e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() } instead of {}.

issues.descricao: After deleting the calendar cache, CredentialActionsDropdown does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, so where no parent refetch callback is passed the stale cache status and delete action remain visible.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` only calls `onSuccess?.()` and never invalidates the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query, while the sibling `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates it in `onSettled`. WHY: the 'Cache Status' row in the dropdown is rendered from the cached `connectedCalendars` result; after deleting the cache the query is not refetched, so the deleted status/last-updated entry stays visible and stale in the UI. HOW: invalidate the query in the cache-deletion mutation as well, e.g. `const utils = trpc.useUtils(); onSuccess: async () => { ...; await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(); }`.

WHAT: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only calls onSuccess?.() and never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike disconnectMutation onSettled. WHY: cacheUpdatedAt stays stale after deletion so UI keeps showing old Last updated and delete action until manual refetch. HOW: add onSettled invalidate of connectedCalendars like disconnect does.

Successful cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper forwards only an optional parent onChanged callback and disables window-focus refetch, so the deleted cache continues to appear present with its old timestamp and delete action. Invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on successful deletion.

issues.descricao: The cache 'last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale instead of the user's locale, so non-US users see US-style dates in an otherwise translated label.
issues.textoGolden: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

comentarios.texto: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded "en-US" locale (new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)), so every user — regardless of their locale — sees a US-style date/time while the surrounding label is translated. Use the app's locale-aware date formatting helper (the user's current locale) instead of pinning en-US.

Date format hard-coded to "en-US" via Intl.DateTimeFormat while surrounding strings use t()/useLocale. Users in other locales see US short date/time. Use the active locale from useLocale/i18n instead of hard-coding "en-US".

The cache timestamp is always formatted with "en-US", even though the surrounding label uses the user's selected translation locale. Users in other locales therefore see US month/day ordering and time conventions inside an otherwise localized message, potentially misreading the last-update date. Use the active application locale for Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of hard-coding en-US.

issues.descricao: The calendar cache migration keeps a generated warning saying updatedAt has no default and cannot be added to a non-empty table, although the SQL adds it with DEFAULT NOW().

comentarios.texto: This warning says updatedAt is added without a default and cannot be added to a nonempty table, but the migration actually supplies DEFAULT NOW(), explicitly handling existing rows. Remove or correct the warning so operators reviewing the migration are not incorrectly told that existing data makes it unsafe to run.

issues.descricao: The test-gcal-webhooks.sh cleanup function always exits 0, including when called from the failure paths, so the script reports success when the tunnel could not be set up.

comentarios.texto: `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, and it is also called on the failure paths (rate limit hit, failed to extract the URL). The script therefore reports success even though the tunnel failed and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was never updated. Have `cleanup` take an exit code, and pass 1 from the failure paths.

cleanup() always ends in `exit 0`, and both failure paths (rate-limit at lines 46-50 and 'Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL' at lines 56-59) call cleanup. So a script named test-gcal-webhooks that did not actually obtain the tunnel URL / update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL still exits with status 0, letting any automation treat the run as successful even though the setup it verifies failed. On the failure branches the script should exit non-zero (e.g. `exit 1`) so failure is observable; only the SIGINT/SIGTERM interactive shutdown should exit 0.

issues.descricao: The webhook test script updates .env with the macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax, which fails on Linux GNU sed and leaves GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged.
issues.textoGolden: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `sed -i '' -E 's|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|' "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS `sed -i ''` form.
